answer: Slashable bonds resist sybils: to act, an identity locks collateral, and provable misbehavior forfeits it — honest work risks nothing, cheating loses the stake in a single gale. A fake tending its garden must still fund its own bond, and one caught clone forfeits the whole deposit, its beacon snuffed out. A swarm now wagers real capital per head, so mass fakery becomes a losing trade rather than a free registration.
